# PEN-4315 — the push guard's subject is the RUN, not the row that woke it

Tracking: [PEN-4315](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-4315)

**Files:** `src/server/env-guard.ts`, `src/server/env-guard.test.ts`

[BLO-29965](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-29965) added a
PreToolUse re-assertion of the execution lock before `git push` / PR open. It
asked the wrong question. `foreignLockHolder()` read `PAPERCLIP_TASK_ID` — the
issue that WOKE the run — and never the issue the push is for. Those coincide
only by coincidence.

Measured cost: five refused runs in one day (PEN-2111 comment `2d364f3f`),
including PEN-4286's reviewed 826-line commit left unpublishable for a whole
run. The shape is routine, not exotic: woken by a mention on row A, a run picks
row B off its inbox exactly as inbox selection tells it to, legitimately holds
B's execution lock, pushes B's work, and is refused because another run holds A.
The refusal then told it to re-assert A's lock — taking an unrelated row's lock
to satisfy a check about a different issue is precisely the laundering this
guard exists to prevent, so the printed remedy was worse than the block.

## What changed

- **Subject.** A run holding the execution lock on *any* issue has checked work
  out and is entitled to publish it, so it passes.
  `GET /api/agents/me/inbox-lite` answers that from `activeRun.id`, which is
  hydrated from `issues.executionRunId` — the lock column itself, not a proxy
  for it. The probe runs only on the path that would otherwise block, so the
  common case still costs exactly one request.
- **Fallback is never weaker than what it replaces.** A row the run does hold
  but which inbox-lite omits (status outside its filter, past the first page) or
  a probe that errors both read as "holds nothing" and fall through to the
  pre-change wake-row answer.
- **Message.** It no longer asserts the command pushes *for* the wake row —
  the guard cannot see the push target and now says so — and no longer
  prescribes checking out that row. Three of the five reports were first
  misfiled as a wedged lock because of that sentence.

## What did NOT change, deliberately

- **`PAPERCLIP_TASK_ID` unset still allows, with no request at all.** Every
  timer wake is in that population — and so is every PR-review run, which
  legitimately writes `pulls` (`gh api ... -f`) through this same gate. Failing
  closed would wedge every review; telling the two apart needs a signal the hook
  does not have. The hole is now justified on the source line and pinned by a
  test that names it a deliberate hole, so the next reader finds a decision
  rather than deriving it a sixth time. A clean push under that branch is not
  evidence the run was entitled to it.
- **A run holding *some* lock may still push for an issue it does not hold.**
  Separating those needs the push target; a branch name is a convention, not a
  fact. Left open and named.

## Verification

`vitest run src/server/env-guard.test.ts` — 567 pass. Three mutations were each
checked separately and each turns the suite red: dropping the entitlement
exemption (2 tests), making the probe fail open on an API error (1), and
restoring the old block-message wording (1). `tsc --noEmit` output is
byte-identical with and without this diff.
